page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / A step too far
title: A step too far
topic: Language for giving someone a verbal warning
description:
New recruit Rachel has been making life difficult for Anna and she's been making some bad business decisions. It's time to give her a warning but who is going to do it and what will they say? How is she going to be disciplined?
This episode focuses on what to say when you need to discipline someone and give them a warning.
phrases: You need to consult me before you contact any of our clients.
These mistakes cannot happen again otherwise I will have to refer the matter to someone higher.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello and welcome back to Tip Top Trading. New recruit Rachel has been making life difficult for Anna; she's been making some bad business decisions. Let's find out how Anna can save the day.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Right, we've definitely got to do something about Rachel… definitely… only, I'm a bit busy at the moment.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Sorting out your dinner date are you Tom?!  So Anna, have you spoken to Paul about this?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes I have, but he didn't do anything.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmm, well he is your boss so I think you've got to speak to him again. Take him some biscuits, that might get his attention.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I'll try

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh and keep notes so you have a record of your conversation.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Denise, you're amazing. But where have the pens gone to?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That is strange – we all seem to be losing our pens. Here, use this old pencil.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna. Are you happy complaining officially about Rachel?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not really but what else can I do? She's been spoiling all the work I've been doing.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes she has. OK, well tell Paul the facts and tell him you want action.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. Right, here goes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Come in.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hi Paul.  I really need to speak to you about Rachel. She really is messing things up…Paul?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Sorry, just counting my biscuits. What were you saying? Rachel? Great girl, isn't she?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No she's not.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Paul, she's already sent out the wrong order and now she's upset our new client. Plus, have you seen the way she dresses? I'm not happy and I think you've got to take some action.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, you're on fire! But stick to the facts, don't get personal about Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well I'm sure Mr Socrates would disagree with you. Look, if she is as bad as you say then I'll give you my permission to discipline her – give her a warning.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What! Me?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You know what's she done wrong so tell her not to do it again…and besides, I've got an important meeting to go to… and they usually have those delicious shortbread biscuits. So …I'll leave it with you then?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What a useless boss!  Anna are you happy about what to do next?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not really. What am I going to say?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It's not easy but keep calm and professional and say to Rachel, "you've made some serious mistakes" and "you need to consult me before you contact any of our clients." Give her a verbal warning saying "These mistakes cannot happen again, otherwise I will have to refer the matter to someone higher." This may lead to disciplinary action but it may be for the best.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh it's all very serious but I suppose I've got to do it.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Anna! Darling! What's wrong? I saw Paul and he said you're in a bit of a mood.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's not a mood Rachel. Can we talk please…now?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Yeah sure. Let's sit here, shall we – not in that chair – that's my favourite.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Rachel, I wanted to let you know that you've made some serious mistakes.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Oh!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You have really upset our new client – and you think it's ok to sell second hand plastic oranges.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Calm down. It's business, darling.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's not good business Rachel. These mistakes cannot happen again. If they do I will have to take matters higher and it could result in disciplinary action.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Oh! You're quite scary for a short girl.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: That was unnecessary! But well done Anna for keeping cool and calm in a difficult situation. Let's hope Rachel has got the message. Here is a reminder of the phrases you could use when giving someone a verbal warning…

transcript.speaker: You've made some serious mistakes.
transcript.text:
You need to consult me before you contact any of our clients.
These mistakes cannot happen again otherwise I will have to refer the matter to someone higher.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Let's find out how Rachel is behaving.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ah hello, Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Tommy boy. Come and give me a hug. Opps!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Our pens! All our pens! You've been stealing them! Rachel!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: What's going on? I say, what are all those pens doing on the floor?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: They're from Rachel's handbag. She's been stealing them!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: What? The company's pens?Right, well, I need to see you in my office please Rachel, now…if you don't mind.

transcript.speaker: Anna/Tom/Denise
transcript.text: Gasp!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So Rachel is the pen thief! What does this mean for her job at Tip Top Trading? Find out next time. Until then, bye!
